## One platform. Multiple services.

Vim, your teams and partners build on the same services. Build once, reuse everywhere: each workflow starts with what the last one connected.

Developer tools

## Work from your terminal and your coding agent.

The Vim Connect CLI signs in as you and changes your account's configuration as reviewable diffs. Each SDK ships a skill, so your agent looks the API up before it writes a line.

In your terminal / coding agent

- **Change configuration safely.** Pull a collection, edit it, see the diff, then push a new version with a note. Published versions never change.
- **Secrets that never print.** Values go in at a hidden prompt. Configs hold an address, and a rotation keeps it, so nothing redeploys.
- **Ready for scripts and CI.** Personal access tokens, a profile per account, and exit codes a pipeline can rely on.
- **A skill per SDK.**`vim-app-sdk-docs` and `vim-backend-sdk-docs` ship inside the packages.

[Get the CLI](https://developer-docs.getvim.ai/docs/connect-cli/) [Use with AI](https://developer-docs.getvim.ai/docs/app-sdk/getting-started/ai-tooling/)

TerminalCICoding agent

```
$ npm i -g @vimconnect/connect-cli
$ vim-connect login
  approve the code in your browser, pick an account

$ vim-connect collections pull <id> --out=mine.json
  # edit mine.json
$ vim-connect collections diff <id> mine.json
  Summary: 2 added, 1 changed
$ vim-connect collections push <id> mine.json \
    --message="Add referral urgency"

$ vim-connect secrets set partner-api \
    --field=clientId --field=clientSecret
  prints each field's address, never its value
```

```
# a personal access token, from Console → Build → Tokens
export VIM_CONNECT_PAT="$VIM_PAT"
export VIM_CONNECT_ACCOUNT_ID="$ACCOUNT_ID"

# show what would change; exits 0 either way
vim-connect collections diff <id> mine.json --html=diff.html

# publish on merge, no prompt
vim-connect collections push <id> mine.json \
  --message="$COMMIT_TITLE" --yes

# exit 1: bad input or no login · exit 2: the API refused
```

```
# copy the skill into your repo
cp -r \
  node_modules/@vimconnect/app-sdk/skills/vim-app-sdk-docs \
  .claude/skills/

# then ask
"Show the open patient's active problems in my app,
and write the one I pick back to the encounter."
```
